brief: One of the first masonry commercial buildings on its block (built 1880-84), long used as the American Legion hall: the original brick front is hidden behind a mid-century slipcover of vertical corrugated metal panels over a recessed modern storefront with dark glass and a single door; the building sits vacant between ornate older brick blocks.

facade.notes: 109 W Second St (Crookston MN, 1882), HABS: a two-storey brick front hidden behind a blank mid-century corrugated-metal slipcover, a recessed glass front below, used as the American Legion hall; ornate brick and stone neighbours on both sides show what is behind; a tiny planter on the sidewalk

why.note: HABS recorded these Main Street buildings before urban-renewal or highway demolition (1970s-80s)
1950s-60s 'modernise Main Street' programmes hid old fronts behind metal screens
